# Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 56 (Bi-Vb Pc56)

**ID:** Bi-Vb Pc56
**Section:** Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga (bi-vb)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 56
**Title (English, from literature):** Spending the rainy season apart from monks
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m1.mul7.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Scholars have noted that Pācittiya 56 creates a significant legal and jurisdictional tension within Vinaya jurisprudence [Hüsken 1997]. Because monks and nuns perform their legal acts (*kamma*) independently, each community must determine its own communal boundary (*sīmā*); yet the requirement that nuns reside in an area inhabited by monks implies that the nuns' *sīmā* coincides with or falls inside that of the monks, contrary to general Vinaya rules against overlapping boundaries [Hüsken 1997]. The commentary (*Samantapāsādikā*) specifically attempts to reconcile this contradiction [Hüsken 1997].

Parallels to this rule are preserved across the surviving Buddhist Vinayas, including the Theravāda Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha and Parivāra, the Dharmaguptaka (Vibhaṅga and Prātimokṣa Pc 143), Mahīśāsaka (Pc 91), Sarvāstivāda (Pc 149 / 150), and Mūlasarvāstivāda (Chinese Pc 128; Tibetan Pc 165) traditions. However, unlike the Theravāda canon, the Mahāsāṃghika-Lokottaravādin *Bhīkṣuṇīvinaya* does not include this injunction among its *pācattika* rules [Bechert et al. 1997]. Computational alignments by DharmaNexus identify shared phrasing with the Tibetan *Bhikṣuṇīvinayavibhaṅga* (D0005) and *Āryasarvāstivādimūlabhikṣuṇīpratimokṣasūtravṛtti* (D4112), as well as extensive internal Pali text reuse with the rains retreat chapter of the Khandhaka (*Vassūpanāyikakkhandhaka*, Kd 3) and adjacent Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga rules including Pc 57, Pc 94, and Pc 95 [DharmaNexus]. The rule has been translated into English by Bhikkhu Brahmali.
